lines.trans: Then the final chance for the dinner game of chance is getting words of cheer from a friend.
Since today is your first shoot, you call a close friend.
And if within one minute you hear cheering words like "fighting" or "do well" from your friend…
the mission succeeds and dinner is provided.
Could I not just do the elephant-trunk spin one more time instead?
Have you decided whom to call?
Oh, unni, I came out for my first shoot on 2 Days & 1 Night right now.
This is on the air right now.
No, I was just wondering if there might be something you wanted to say to me.
Mission failed!

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

meanings.note: The time of day from late afternoon into night.
Short for 저녁 식사 or 저녁밥.

examples.trans: Did you eat dinner?
Let's meet this evening.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그럼 저녁 식사 복불복 마지막 찬스는 친구에게 응원 받기입니다.
examples.trans: Then the final chance for the dinner game of chance is getting words of cheer from a friend.
Here the word for 'meal' is key.

examples.text: 가면 저녁밥 복불복 게임 하실 겁니다.
examples.trans: Once we arrive, you will play a game of chance for dinner.
The topic of game of luck came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Can modify a following noun directly (마지막 촬영지) or take 으로 (마지막으로, 'finally').

examples.trans: Today is the last day.
Please ask the final question.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그럼 저녁 식사 복불복 마지막 찬스는 친구에게 응원 받기입니다.
examples.trans: Then the final chance for the dinner game of chance is getting words of cheer from a friend.
Here the word for 'as for the chance' is key.

meanings.note: Primary meaning: a friend or peer.

meanings.en: that person / kid (referring to someone younger)
meanings.note: Older speakers often refer to a younger person or celebrity as 그 친구.

examples.trans: I watched a movie with a friend today.
That kid really sings well.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그럼 저녁 식사 복불복 마지막 찬스는 친구에게 응원 받기입니다.
examples.trans: Then the final chance for the dinner game of chance is getting words of cheer from a friend.
Here the word for 'cheering, support' is key.

meanings.note: Used for gifts, money, messages, or documents.

examples.trans: I received a birthday present.
Please answer the phone.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.note: Prenoun (determiner) placed directly before a noun

examples.trans: Today is my first day at work.
The first snow fell.
Did you hear about this filming too?
I was busy today because of filming too.

meanings.en: to be close, on good terms
meanings.note: Used for close personal relationships; often paired with -와/과 or -하고 ('with').

examples.trans: We are very close.
Are you close with that actor?

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word for telephone.

examples.trans: A phone call came.
I will hang up the phone.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 1분 안에 친구가 파이팅 또는 잘해라는 응원의 말을 들으면,
examples.trans: And if within one minute you hear cheering words like "fighting" or "do well" from your friend…
Here the word for 'one minute' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.text: 1분 안에 친구가 파이팅 또는 잘해라는 응원의 말을 들으면,
examples.trans: And if within one minute you hear cheering words like "fighting" or "do well" from your friend…
Here the word for 'fighting!, go for it!' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 1분 안에 친구가 파이팅 또는 잘해라는 응원의 말을 들으면,
examples.trans: And if within one minute you hear cheering words like "fighting" or "do well" from your friend…
Here the word for 'or' is key.

meanings.note: verb do well

examples.trans: Study well.
You did well.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

meanings.note: verb listen

examples.trans: Listen well.
Listen to a song.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: the mission succeeds and dinner is provided.
Here the word for 'mission' is key.

examples.text: 예상을 전혀 못 한 것 같고 작전으로는 성공인데 희한하네.
examples.trans: She didn't expect it at all, so the operation succeeded, yet something feels odd.
The topic of is a success, though came up during this shoot.

examples.text: 가면 저녁밥 복불복 게임 하실 겁니다.
examples.trans: Once we arrive, you will play a game of chance for dinner.
The topic of evening meal, dinner came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: the mission succeeds and dinner is provided.
This expression comes from 'is provided'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 코끼리 코 한 번 더 하면 안 되나?
examples.trans: Could I not just do the elephant-trunk spin one more time instead?
Here the word for 'elephant' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 코끼리 코 한 번 더 하면 안 되나?
examples.trans: Could I not just do the elephant-trunk spin one more time instead?
Here the word for 'nose, trunk' is key.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

meanings.note: Used before adjectives or verbs.

examples.trans: Please give me a little more.
It's further away.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.en: to initiate (conversation), to hang, to call
meanings.note: Used in 말을 걸다 (to strike up a conversation) or 전화를 걸다 (to make a call).

examples.trans: I started a conversation.
I started a conversation. (2)

meanings.note: Honorific noun and counter for people, used instead of 사람.

examples.trans: That person over there is our teacher.
How many people are in your party?

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.trans: Have you decided whom to call?
This expression comes from 'has it been decided?'.

meanings.note: Spontaneous exclamation of mild surprise or puzzlement when noticing something unexpected. RR: eo.

examples.trans: Huh? Where is my phone?
Oh? It is raining.
Did you hear about this older sister, idol?
I was busy today because of older sister, idol.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.
Did you hear about this 1 night?
I was busy today because of 1 night.
Did you hear about this 2 days?
I was busy today because of 2 days.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

meanings.note: Refers to both the act of broadcasting and the aired program itself.

examples.trans: That program airs on Sunday evening.
Please turn off your phone during the broadcast.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Mission failed!
Here the word for 'failure!' is key.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
